summary: I tested the 5.839 d, 180 ppm signal on TOI-266 (HIP 8152) against the two known planets (10.751 d, 19.606 d), every literature hit, ExoFOP, the blend space, the centroids, TRICERATOPS's contrast-curve clamp and star list, and the light curve's artefacts. It is no harmonic or beat alias of b or c. No paper, ExoFOP row or catalogue reports anything at this period. The old TOI-266.02 periods (6.19 d, 6.54 d) are superseded aliases of planet c and share no transit with it. On the star the blend space looks closed, the centroid offsets over 15 arcsec are noise, and TRICERATOPS's pass leans neither on the clamp nor on a duplicate. The dip shows in SAP and PDCSAP in all four sectors and not in the background. But no season can be held out, and the search found it just 3% above the null threshold, so the TESS data can't replicate it. I rate that a hold.

findings.claim: The public TESS data can't replicate the transit independently of the period search: every held-out season is underpowered and the search found it just above the null threshold, so its reality rests on the full four-sector fold alone.
findings.evidence: checks.json (drafts/m3-r2/164767175-1) holdout: all four seasons 'underpowered', expected_snr 3.32, 3.08, 3.82 and 2.98 against [holdout] min_expected_snr 4.0 (criteria/vet-v3.toml), outcome inconclusive. The held-out depths 134 +- 56, 126 +- 72, 228 +- 43 and 221 +- 67 ppm (tensions 0.85, 1.19, 1.11, 0.29) agree but are not a test. Search: SDE 20.887 ($SEARCH_RUN/signals.parquet, tic 164767175, rank 1) against the threshold 20.245 ($THRESHOLD_RUN/threshold.json, expected_false_alarms 1.03 over n_sample 30195). Of the 19 vetted signals it has the second-lowest SDE and the lowest depth_snr (9.60). Per sector (checks.json sector_depth, beta-scaled): S3 163 +- 64, S30 145 +- 62, S97 273 +- 43, S107 178 +- 62 ppm; without S97 the weighted mean is 162 +- 36 ppm (4.5 sigma). For reality, short of replication: signal_present is 7.51 sigma. The vet's own statistic at 82 independent phase offsets of the same period has sd 1.15 and max 2.24, so the real value is 6.65 sd. The best phase at each of 300 random periods from 3 to 9 d reaches at most 4.26 (/tmp/t13/164767175-1/sp_scramble.py, output sp_scramble.out; run as /tmp/t13/heavy.sh uv run python /tmp/t13/164767175-1/sp_scramble.py from ~/code/tess-hunt). On a local-baseline statistic it is 4.9 sd of its phase nulls (pertransit.py, pertransit.out). Akana Murphy et al. 2023 (arXiv 2306.16587, section 6.1.2) ran BLS on S3 and S30 after masking b and c and found no further transit-like event, which fits S3 and S30 holding about 3 sigma of it. tess-point gives no upcoming sector (checks.json upcoming_sectors []). What would decide: photometry at the predicted times precise to about 50 ppm per 3-hour transit, either CHEOPS (new visits, or the 2022 archival HIP 8152 visits that confirmed planet c if one covers a predicted transit) or a future TESS 2-min sector. Ground photometry can't reach 180 ppm. A fit of the public HIRES (94) and ESPRESSO (26) RVs at P 5.83926 d and the transit phase would add a mass limit but would not decide alone: K is about 1.2 m/s for a 3 Earth-mass planet (K = 28.4 m/s x Mp/MJ x (P/1 yr)^(-1/3) x (M*/Msun)^(-2/3), M* 0.84).

refuters.reason:
Every number F1 rests on reproduces. Scratch is in /tmp/t13/164767175-1/refute-F1-reproduce/.

1) Holdout. The draft checks.json is byte-identical to $VET2_RUN/signals/164767175-1/checks.json (cmp). Its holdout check reports all four seasons as "underpowered", with expected_snr 3.32, 3.08, 3.82 and 2.98. Depths are 134 +- 56, 126 +- 72, 228 +- 43 and 221 +- 67 ppm, tensions 0.85, 1.19, 1.11 and 0.29. Outcome is inconclusive ("0 season(s) could be tested; need 2"). criteria/vet-v3.toml [holdout] sets min_expected_snr = 4.0. upcoming_sectors is [].

2) Search vs threshold. In $SEARCH_RUN/signals.parquet, tic 164767175 rank 1 has sde 20.8865 and depth_snr 9.603. $THRESHOLD_RUN/threshold.json has threshold 20.2449, expected_false_alarms 1.029 and n_sample 30195. My script (refute-F1-reproduce/sde.py) ranked the 19 names under $VET2_RUN/signals. This signal has the second-lowest SDE (only 296819076-1 is lower, at 20.72) and the lowest depth_snr (next is 103312990-1 at 11.97).

3) Sector depths. checks.json sector_depth gives S3 163 +- 64, S30 145 +- 62, S97 273 +- 43 and S107 178 +- 62 ppm. The inverse-variance mean without S97 is 162.1 +- 36.2 ppm (4.48 sigma). All four combine to 208.1 +- 27.7, the same as signal_present's err of 27.7 ppm, so the errors are the beta-scaled ones. signal_present snr is 7.509.

4) Phase and period nulls. Rerun: `/tmp/t13/heavy.sh uv run python /tmp/t13/164767175-1/sp_scramble.py` from ~/code/tess-hunt, exit 0. It reproduced the original output exactly: snr 7.51 with n 830; 82 phase offsets with sd 1.15 and max 2.24; real value 6.65 sd; 300 random periods with max 4.26 at P = 7.8132. The pertransit.py rerun through heavy.sh produced output identical to pertransit.out (diff empty): 204.3 ppm = 4.89 sd of the 2000-offset phase scramble.

5) Literature. Akana Murphy et al. 2023 (papers/2306.16587.pdf.txt), section 6.1.2, says they masked b and c, ran another BLS and "found no additional transit-like events". Line 339 lists HIP 8152 sectors 3 and 30. Table 4 lists 94 Keck-HIRES RVs. Section 10.1 says CHEOPS observed a transit of c in 2022-Aug. papers/2605.27002v1.html.txt lists 26 ESPRESSO RVs for TOI-266 (TIC 164767175) and M* 0.838.

6) K. The finding's formula with Mp = 3 Earth masses, P = 5.83926 d and M* = 0.84 gives K = 1.195 m/s.

One discrepancy, too small to refute: 2605.27002 says Akana Murphy used "95 RVs" from HIRES, while Akana Murphy's own Table 4 says 94. The finding's 94 matches the primary source.

Not refuted. The finding reads the rules correctly, and a hold fits the brief. One part of its "what would decide" needs correcting.

1. Holdout is read correctly. In src/tess_hunt/checks/holdout.py, line 186 marks a season "underpowered" when expected/err < [holdout] min_expected_snr (4.0 in criteria/vet-v3.toml). Only "predicted" or "missed" seasons count as tested, and fewer than 2 tested seasons makes the check inconclusive. Running python3 over drafts/m3-r2/164767175-1/checks.json gives all four seasons underpowered, at expected_snr 3.32, 3.08, 3.82 and 2.98, each with training_seasons_with_transits 3 (so decision 0035 is not the cause). The outcome is "inconclusive: 0 season(s) could be tested; need 2". No sector is timing-suspect (dropped_suspect is [], all four sectors are SPOC 120 s) and there is one family (pdcsap), so decisions 0022 and 0023 change nothing. checks-with-suspect.json gives the same outcome. "Agree but are not a test" matches the code comment at line 187 ("absence proves nothing") and decision 0004.

2. "Its reality rests on the full fold alone" matches decision 0017. signal_present on the full fold is the only check that asks whether a dip exists (7.51 sigma >= min_snr 7.0). 0017 says odd/even, secondary and sector depth pass pure noise. Their passes therefore add no evidence for reality.

3. The threshold is read correctly. Decision 0019 defines the threshold as the highest null SDE that survives the false-alarm tests, and expected_false_alarms as n_sample over the null's size. threshold.json gives threshold 20.245, expected_false_alarms 1.029, n_sample 30195, n_null_stars 29343. signals.parquet in $SEARCH_RUN has tic 164767175, rank 1, SDE 20.887 and depth_snr 9.60. Of the 19 signals in $VET2_RUN/signals it is the second-lowest SDE (after 296819076-1 at 20.72) and the lowest depth_snr.

4. A hold fits the rules. Bar 1 of design section 4.9 and decision 0028 require every vet-v3 check to pass, so an inconclusive holdout already blocks a pass. Decisions 0028 and 0031 say an inconclusive at low SNR kills nothing. With no kill, the signal can only be held, and the finding supplies the deciding evidence a held call needs. In calls.py, lines 171 and 172 require deciding_evidence to be non-empty text only, so naming CHEOPS, which is not on the brief's list of examples, is allowed. The lens is right: design sections 4.7 and 4.8 put held-out seasons under real and new. upcoming_sectors [] matches decision 0024 and design 4.1 ("none through S134").

5. The caveats do not change the verdict, but they should go to the maintainer:
   - "A future TESS 2-min sector" does not meet the finding's own bar of about 50 ppm per 3-hour transit. Sector depth errors in checks.json are 43 to 64 ppm per sector, which is about 110 to 125 ppm per transit's core at 45 core cadences per transit. Under the [holdout] rule, a new single-sector season would itself be underpowered: S3, S30 and S107 alone give expected_snr 3.3, 3.1 and 3.0. CHEOPS stays as a valid decider, so the hold still names one.
   - The finding misses S108. tess-point (tess_stars2px_function_entry at the star's checks.json position) places the star in S107 and S108. S108 is already observed but not yet public: a listing of stpubdata/tess/public/tid/s0108/ returns KeyCount 0 for this star and for every star. It is the nearest new TESS data. Folded into season 3, it would raise that season to an expected SNR of about 4.2, which by itself still leaves fewer than two seasons tested.

findings.claim: No artefact found: the dip is in SAP and PDCSAP in every sector, it is not in the background, no single transit carries it, and no momentum dump falls inside a transit that carries depth.
findings.evidence: The four SPOC 2-min files fetched from stpubdata (sha256 equal to checks.json sources) are in /tmp/t13/164767175-1/fits. bkg.py (output bkg.out) folds the core minus the local baseline on quality-0 cadences, with b and c masked, against 60 phase offsets, giving PDCSAP / SAP / SAP_BKG in ppm of the star: S3 -112 / -46 / -33 (z -1.34 / -0.49 / -0.20); S30 -154 / -256 / -41 (z -1.67 / -1.86 / -0.34); S97 -231 / -247 / -282 (z -4.11 / -2.12 / -0.75); S107 -198 / -160 / -422 (z -2.55 / -2.03 / -0.66). The background's null sd is 1026 to 3145 ppm, so it shows no feature at the transit. quality.py (quality.out) gives momentum dumps (bit 32): only S3 epoch 3 has one inside the transit window, 1.6 h before mid-transit, and that transit shows -18.5 ppm (no dip). S107 epoch 496's dump is 5.3 h after mid-transit. pertransit.py (pertransit.out) gives a leave-one-transit-out SNR of 7.14 to 7.90 over 19 transits; S97 holds 8 of them. No timing-suspect or QLP sector: families pdcsap only, dropped_suspect []; CROWDSAP 0.999 to 1.000.

findings.claim: Nothing published or catalogued sits at or near 5.839 d: the period is no harmonic or beat alias of HIP 8152 b or c, and the 6.54, 6.548 and 6.19 d rows for TOI-266.02 are superseded aliases of planet c that share no transit with this signal.
findings.evidence: b/P = 1.8412 and c/P = 3.3576, far from novelty's harmonics (1, 0.5, 2, 1/3, 3). The nearest i/b + j/c with |i|, |j| <= 4 is 4/b - 4/c = 5.951 d, 1.9% off. ExoFOP live JSON (/tmp/t13/164767175-1/exofop.json): the 6.54 d and 6.548 d user rows were uploaded by 'eastman' on 2019-05-10 and 2019-05-31 at epoch 2458398.288, planet c's S3 transit (BTJD 1398.29). c/3 is 6.535 d, and the ratio to ours is 1.120. SPOC's original TOI-266.02 period was 6.19 d, Tc 1392.10 (Akana Murphy et al. 2023, arXiv 2306.16587 section 6.1.2: 'spuriously reported'). The Triple-9 catalogue lists it at 6.191320 d, epoch 2458392.105, 345 ppm, PC (VizieR J/MNRAS/513/102). Its ratio to ours is 1.060. Its S3 events nearest ours are 1404.488 against our 1404.777 (6.9 h apart), and c's 1398.287 against our 1398.938 (15.6 h). SPOC TCE s0001-s0036-02 (10.9911 d, t0 1387.3) runs through c's two transits (1398.29, 2123.70) and our epochs 0 and 128 (checks.json catalogued overlaps [0, 128]). Its ratio is 1.882, not a match: it is SPOC's alias fit of c. Dynamite predictions for TOI-266 are 4.93 d and 19.8 d (Dietrich and Apai 2020), and 3.55, 21.2, 18.5 and 20.3 d (Turtelboom et al. 2025, arXiv 2409.03852, Tables 1 to 4). None is near 5.84 d, and the 2025 paper lists no new TOI on the star since 2020. Hobson et al. 2026 (arXiv 2605.27002, section 3.3.3) prefer two circular planets on S3, S30, ESPRESSO and HIRES. ExoFOP has no CTOI. The star is a known planet host, so the papers in hits_flagged all name it as one; none reports a third signal.

findings.claim: The centroid offsets beyond 15 arcsec in S30, S97 and S107 are noise around the target, not an off-target source; triage's pass on S3 agrees with the other sectors' pixels.
findings.evidence: I refitted triage's saved difference images ($TRIAGE_RUN tdi pickles) with the pixel diagnosis's /tmp/pixel-diag/sector_detail.py on /tmp/t13/164767175-1/jobs_pix.json. Output is in pix_detail.json, summarized by pix_summary.py in pix_summary.out. Every rebuilt image reproduces the saved one. Fits: S3 2.1 arcsec (E +1.3, N -1.6), quality 0.84; S30 17.8 (E +12.5, N +12.6), q 0.65; S97 22.9 (E +1.7, N -22.8), q 0.35; S107 28.6 (E +20.8, N +19.6), q 0.28. In S97 and S107, 10 and 11 of 16 null images reach the fit's quality. The quality-weighted mean fit sits 7.7 arcsec from the target, with a sky scatter of 18.2 arcsec, which is 0.84 standard errors. The pixel diagnosis (results/benchmarks/pixel-check-diagnosis-2026-10-20.md) gives 7.8 to 26.6 for real off-target sources and at most 1.4 for unsaturated known planets. The target's 3 x 3 box shows the loss against its nulls at z 4.79 (S3), 3.41 (S97), 1.42 (S30) and 0.16 (S107). No catalogued star but the target lies within 42 arcsec of any fit. S3 is not timing-suspect.

findings.claim: The blend space looks closed: no Gaia source within 67 arcsec, no companion in speckle or AO imaging, no astrometric or WDS sign of one, and TRICERATOPS gave every other star zero depth.
findings.evidence: A Gaia DR3 TAP cone of 120 arcsec around the target (gea.esac.esa.int tap-server sync, gaiadr3.gaia_source CONTAINS CIRCLE(26.20925, -18.40138, 0.0333)) finds the nearest other source at 67.6 arcsec (G 19.63, BP-RP 2.56), then 81.8 (G 17.80) and 90.4 (G 15.39). That fits the empty neighbours.csv (1 arcmin cone). The 67.6 arcsec star is probably TRICERATOPS's TIC 164767177 (T 18.68, 69.7 arcsec at J2000), given tdepth 0. TRICERATOPS lists 29 stars, all but the target at tdepth 0, with NFPP 0 in all 10 runs and hosts []. Target RUWE 0.83; Gaia DR3 non_single_star 0. Kervella et al. 2019 (VizieR J/A+A/623/A72, HIP 8152): BinH 0, BinG2 0, PMaG2 S/N 1.48. Zhang et al. 2024 (arXiv 2310.03299, Table 5): SNR_G 0.23. WDS (VizieR B/wds/wds) has nothing within 120 arcsec. ExoFOP imaging (literature.json): 'Alopeke 4.49 and 6.47 mag at 0.5 arcsec, HRCam 7.4 mag at 1 arcsec, PHARO Br-gamma 6.169 mag at 0.5 arcsec; Akana Murphy et al. 2023 section 3.2.1 reports no stellar companions; ExoFOP stellar_companions is empty. Howard et al. 2022 (VizieR J/MNRAS/512/L60): 0 flares in 39.6 d, Binarity 0. Decision 0032's binary 20 to 25 arcsec out can't arise, with nothing within 67 arcsec.

findings.claim: TRICERATOPS's pass leans on neither the contrast-curve clamp nor a TIC duplicate: NFPP does not use the curves, and the clamp reaches only companions too faint to host the dip.
findings.evidence: probs.csv: TP 0.9146, PTP 0.0641, DTP 0.00013. STP 0.0211 is 96% of the mean FPP 0.022. SEB 1.8e-6, SEBx2P 1.7e-6, BEB 2.5e-5, BEBx2P 1.7e-5, every other scenario below 1e-11. The margin to the 0.5 bar is 0.478. NFPP comes from TIC stars that calc_depths gave tdepth 0, so contrast curves don't enter it. In triceratops funcs.py:533, np.interp gives a dmag beyond a curve's deepest point that curve's widest separation, and limiting_separation (funcs.py:577) takes the minimum over curves. The converted curves ($TRIC2_RUN/contrast) reach PHARO K 8.53 mag by 1.19 arcsec and 9.27 at 9.857, and 832 nm 8.21 at 1.175. The 562 nm and NESSI curves stop at 4.75, 6.27 and 4.83 mag by 1.2. So the clamp can tighten an exclusion beyond what was measured only for companions fainter than K 8.53, outside 1.19 arcsec. A companion that could host the dip needs TESS dmag <= 9.36 (depth <= 1), and a redder bound star has a smaller K contrast than TESS contrast, so PHARO's measured part decides for every possible host. At TESS dmag 8.21 a host already needs a 35% eclipse. No validated label (FPP 0.022 > 0.015). The star list (MAST TIC query, /tmp/t13/164767175-1/tic_all.json) holds no DUPLICATE disposition. TIC 508568626 (T 16.40) carries duplicate_id 164767179 (SPLIT, T 13.40); both are about 172 arcsec out with tdepth 0. TIC 10000443581 and 10000443584 are 2MASS extended sources (objType EXTENDED) counted as stars, also at tdepth 0. NFPP is 0 either way, and 0032's ephemeris sensitivity can't move an NFPP made of zero-depth stars.

findings.claim: Published RVs exclude an eclipsing binary on the target, and the shape, secondary, odd/even, density and radius all read as a small planet.
findings.evidence: Hobson et al. 2026 (arXiv 2605.27002, Table 5 and section 3.3.3): K_b 2.42 +- 0.30 and K_c 2.41 +- 0.33 m/s, ESPRESSO jitter 1.42 m/s over 26 RVs. TKS XX (arXiv 2405.14786): HIRES jitter 3.12 m/s over 94 RVs. A companion of 0.08 solar masses on a 5.84 d orbit would give K near 10 km/s, so only blends are left (F5, F6). ModShift (triage evidence 164767175-1.json): the secondary is 2.98 sigma at phase 0.649 (65 +- 22 ppm), below the positive 3.73 sigma event at 0.389 (Fred 1.42). LEO-Vetter gives PC with no FA or FP test failed. A 1.3 Earth-radius planet's own occultation would be far below 65 ppm, so the secondary is noise. odd_even 1.1 sigma; phase 0.5 at -0.74 sigma; grazing probability 0.25%; b 0.48 (flat-prior fit) and 0.21 (density prior); density tension 1.4 sigma (0.81 against the TIC's 1.88 g/cm3); Rp 1.26 to 1.29 Earth radii. The search's other signal on the star, 1.3890 d (SDE 9.2, 65 ppm), sits at ratio 4.204, not an EB pair.

findings.claim: Hits not flagged whose dismissal isn't obvious from the title: none names the star as an eclipsing binary, variable or multiple, or reports a signal near 5.84 d.
findings.evidence: Bonomo et al. 2025, 'Cold Jupiters and small planets' (doi 10.1051/0004-6361/202452523, arXiv 2505.20035): the PDF text never names HIP 8152 or TOI-266 (grep of papers/2505.20035.pdf.txt). OpenAlex matched it on both names, probably from a sample table. SWEET-Cat (arXiv 2409.11965) and 'The Gaia spectroscopic catalogue of exoplanets and host stars' (arXiv 2505.22205): catalogue papers whose text never names the star (grep_pdfs.py), linked by SIMBAD through their tables. Kervella et al. 2019 (arXiv 1811.08902) and Brandt 2021 (arXiv 2105.11662): proper-motion-anomaly catalogues. Kervella's row for HIP 8152 has BinH 0 and BinG2 0 (F5). 'La pensee maternaliste' (OpenAlex W1530622523) is a false match on 'TOI-266'. The Hipparcos, RAVE, PASTEL, uvby, JSDC and Gaia red-clump papers are stellar catalogues, plain from their titles.
